component_rule: Access verification and semantic/entity typing are tracked independently; a verified access route does not imply completed entity typing.

records.note: Clima Gerais integrates territorial climate-vulnerability indicators and visualization; current canonical route is viewer-oriented.
IDE-SISEMA is a state spatial-data infrastructure/catalog-viewer; dataset identity remains layer-specific.
AdaptaBrasil is a national climate-impact information and analysis system; indicators are the scientific data objects, while the canonical route is primarily interactive.
SIRENE is the official Brazilian information system for national greenhouse-gas emissions and removals; inventories and series are the scientific data objects.
CEMADEN is a national monitoring and warning center; station series, monitoring products and alerts are distinct data families rather than one dataset.
PANORAMA/CENSIPAM integrates Amazon territorial monitoring, geospatial data and services; access varies by product/service.
UrbVerde is an academic territorial-intelligence platform exposing derived urban socioenvironmental indicators primarily through web visualization/reports.
dados.gov.br is Brazil's national public-data catalog; it indexes datasets and distributions published by many agencies and is not itself one scientific dataset.
GBIF is a global biodiversity data infrastructure/network; occurrence, checklist and sampling-event datasets retain publisher-specific provenance.
MapBiomas Brasil is a collaborative data-production initiative/network with multiple scientific data families and platform routes; it is not a single dataset.
TerraBrasilis is INPE's geospatial data platform for monitoring programs such as PRODES and DETER; those programs/products remain distinct scientific data families.
Programa Queimadas is an operational satellite-monitoring program with multiple data families including fire detections, fire risk and burned-area products.
speciesLink is a network integrating records from biological collections; dataset and collection provenance remains source-specific.

SiBBr is Brazil's national biodiversity information infrastructure; the canonical DR route remains a generic homepage, so access remains E until a specific aggregate acquisition route is demonstrated.
BDiA is an IBGE thematic environmental database covering geology, geomorphology, soils and vegetation; individual layers/collections are the data objects.
CNUC is the official national register of protected areas under SNUC; cadastral records and spatial boundaries are its principal data objects.
SNIRH/HidroWeb is a national water-resources information system and access tool; hydrometeorological station series are the scientific data objects.
BDMEP is INMET's meteorological database providing historical station observations; station/time-variable selections define the extracted datasets.
Google Earth Engine Data Catalog indexes many third-party geospatial datasets and provides processing/export infrastructure; dataset provenance remains provider-specific.
AppEEARS is a data extraction service for spatial/temporal/layer subsets across multiple federal archives; it is an access service, not a dataset family.
Copernicus Climate Data Store is a climate-data catalog and access service; individual catalog datasets retain their own identity, provenance and licence.
Climate Data Guide curates expert descriptions/evaluations and links to climate datasets; it normally does not host the underlying datasets.
GBIF IPT is publishing software, not an aggregated data-access entity.
Global Forest Watch is a monitoring/data platform aggregating layers from multiple providers; provenance remains layer-specific.
Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem is an access/processing infrastructure exposing many mission datasets and services, not one dataset.
Project COSMOS is a bibliometric climate-research database with public analytical products but no open full-database download.
